publish.title: The rule of 72: how long does money take to double?
publish.description: A rule of thumb for doubling time, with four examples. Education, not financial advice.

scenes.headline: The rule of 72
scenes.narration: Here is a quick way to estimate how long money takes to double.

scenes.headline: Divide 72 by the rate
scenes.narration: Divide seventy-two by the yearly growth rate. The answer is roughly the number of years it takes to double.

definition.meaning: Years to double is about 72 divided by the annual rate of return, as a percentage.

scenes.headline: Years to double
scenes.narration: At three percent it takes about twenty-four years. At six percent, twelve. At nine percent, eight. At twelve percent, six.

scenes.headline: It works on debt too
scenes.narration: The same rule shows how fast a debt can double at a given interest rate, if nothing is paid off.

scenes.headline: An estimate, not a promise
scenes.narration: Real returns change from year to year and are never guaranteed. This is a rule of thumb, not financial advice.

scenes.headline: Try your own numbers
scenes.narration: Pick a rate you read about and divide it into seventy-two.
